content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"Warrior Systems <$5M is a procurement program run by U.S. Special Operations Command (SOCOM), funded through the Procurement, Defense-Wide account.","citation":{"fact_id":"74731d4c3273f61a"}},{"text":"The program funds the procurement, rapid fielding, and associated costs of specialized equipment for Special Operations Forces (SOF) in areas such as communications, weapons, soldier protection and survival systems, Multi-Mission Electronic Counter Measures (MM-ECM), Counter Uncrewed Systems (CUxS), and Visual Augmentation Systems (VAS) including optics, lasers, and simulators.","citation":{"fact_id":"849ab8bb5c839da3"}},{"text":"The stated goal is to improve Special Operations Forces warfighting capabilities by continuing the procurement of smaller, lighter, more efficient, and more robust equipment tailored to SO-peculiar (SO-p, meaning special-operations-specific) requirements.","citation":{"fact_id":"849ab8bb5c839da3"}},{"text":"The FY 2026 request for Warrior Systems includes $303.991 million of discretionary funding and $80.055 million of mandatory (reconciliation) funding, for a total of $384.046 million.","citation":{"fact_id":"9957b67472021bc3"}},{"text":"The portfolio covers a wide range of individual programs, including the Satellite Deployable Node (SDN) family of deployable satellite communications systems that give deployed SOF users high-capacity voice, data, and video connectivity.","citation":{"fact_id":"9957b67472021bc3"}},{"text":"The Weapons program (Program Number 709) provides SOF operators with common and emerging caliber weapons — including rifles, sniper rifles, machine guns, and handguns — able to engage targets at ranges up to 2,000 meters.","citation":{"fact_id":"9957b67472021bc3"}},{"text":"The Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) program provides medical devices and equipment for treating casualties in support of forward-deployed SOF, including a Brain Health Blast Exposure Monitoring (BEMO) system.","citation":{"fact_id":"9957b67472021bc3"}},{"text":"The Counter Uncrewed Systems (CUxS) program, formerly Counter Unmanned Aerial Systems (CUAS), enhances the SOF operator's ability to detect, identify, track, deter, defeat, and exploit uncrewed system threats across air, ground, and maritime domains.","citation":{"fact_id":"9957b67472021bc3"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"For FY 2024, the program recorded actual spending of $600.69 million (in USD thousands, $600,690) in the Procurement, Defense-Wide account.","citation":{"fact_id":"74731d4c3273f61a"}},{"text":"The FY 2025 enacted amount was $402.712 million ($402,712 thousand).","citation":{"fact_id":"0b967cdc17f2d35b"}},{"text":"The FY 2026 total request is $384.046 million ($384,046 thousand), which is lower than both the FY 2024 actual and FY 2025 enacted amounts.","citation":{"fact_id":"83f87d1480a040c0"}},{"text":"The FY 2026 total is split between a $303.991 million discretionary request and an $80.055 million reconciliation (mandatory) request.","citation":{"fact_id":"ecedc02b7b0f4fee"}},{"text":"The FY 2026 reconciliation portion alone amounts to $80.055 million ($80,055 thousand).","citation":{"fact_id":"8d2ff5e61b7405db"}},{"text":"Because the program bundles many small equipment lines, changes hit a broad set of SOF capabilities at once — for example, the FY 2025-to-FY 2026 decrease of $6.266 million for the SDN program reflects a command decision to no longer invest in the SDN-Heavy system.","citation":{"fact_id":"9957b67472021bc3"}},{"text":"The TCCC line's FY 2025-to-FY 2026 increase of $9.352 million supports adoption and continued fielding of Brain Health Blast Exposure Monitoring systems for SOF personnel at risk of blast overpressure exposure — procuring 11,314 blast sensor monitoring devices in the base program.","citation":{"fact_id":"9957b67472021bc3"}},{"text":"In FY 2024 the line received Ukraine Replacement Transfer funding for CUxS ($10.439 million), VAS ($15.702 million), Weapons ($1.782 million), and Remote Advise and Assist / Virtual Accompany Kit ($4.051 million).","citation":{"fact_id":"849ab8bb5c839da3"}},{"text":"In FY 2024 the line also received Congressional Add funding, including CUAS group 3 defeat acceleration ($40.613 million), enhanced night vision devices ($2.000 million), and resilient waveform capability ($5.000 million).","citation":{"fact_id":"849ab8bb5c839da3"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"The program is managed by U.S. Special Operations Command (SOCOM).","citation":{"fact_id":"74731d4c3273f61a"}},{"text":"Beginning in FY 2026, the Tactical Local Area Network (TACLAN) and Fly-Away Broadcasting System (FABS) programs transitioned their funding from the P-1 Line Item Other Items <$5M into this Warrior Systems <$5M line item.","citation":{"fact_id":"849ab8bb5c839da3"}},{"text":"Classified portions of the program totaled $4.877 million in FY 2024, $14.391 million in FY 2025, and $12.201 million in FY 2026, with details provided under separate cover.","citation":{"fact_id":"849ab8bb5c839da3"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
